page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance featuring two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 96 GB VRAM. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H x86_64 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz. It includes 375.0 GB of system memory, yielding 11.72 GB per core, and is equipped with 2200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in LLM inference, with prompt processing speeds reaching 13643.47 tokens per second and text generation at 348.06 tokens per second for a small 135M model. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing achieves 6275.36 tokens per second and text generation reaches 141.42 tokens per second. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 62892.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 64768.69. Memory bandwidth is strong for read-only operations, measuring 4985.78 GB/sec for small blocks and 211.9 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec.

The server offers high resource density by combining massive GPU memory with substantial system RAM and local NVMe storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring simultaneous compute and memory capacity. However, single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2209.29, indicating that single-threaded tasks may limit overall throughput. This hardware profile is suited for LLM inference, machine learning workloads, database operations, and data-intensive processing tasks.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated server configured with two NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPUs delivering 96 GB of total VRAM. It features an Intel Xeon 6448H x86_64 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores, 375.0 GB of system memory, and 2200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference, with prompt processing for a 7B model reaching 6275.36 tokens per second. Multi-core CPU performance and database operations are strong, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 64768.69 and a Redis SET throughput of 70.17 million operations per second. While read-only memory bandwidth is strong, large-block write bandwidth and single-core CPU performance are average. This instance is designed for machine learning inference, database operations, and parallel data processing workloads.
